name: matmul
axis: 2D matrix multiply over flat row-major arrays — cache behaviour on a 3-deep loop nest plus the per-access bounds check on the innermost read/modify/write
n: N=600 (600x600 f64), ROUNDS=3 (648M innermost iterations; 2.88MB per matrix, 8.6MB working set)
nPython: N=230, ROUNDS=3 (work is cubic in N, so this is a (600/230)^3 = 17.8x reduction; multiply Python's wall time by 17.8 to compare)
notes: i-k-j order (cache-friendly: the innermost loop walks contiguous rows of B and C). ROUNDS repeats the multiply ACCUMULATING into the same C without re-zeroing, so the work is exactly linear in ROUNDS and no round can be CSE'd away. The f64 sum is reduced to an integer as (s*1000) as i64 / Math.trunc / int() so all four print a byte-identical checksum without depending on float formatting; the operation order is identical in all four so the f64 sums are bit-identical. Scale-verified by doubling ROUNDS: vl 1.92x, rs 2.08x, js 1.82x, py 2.08x. opt.vl is a hand-optimized attempt that measures a WASH - see its header comment.

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 105ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 6% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.rustVectorised: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT — rustc -O AUTO-VECTORISES this loop and no meta note said so. Confirmed by disassembling `main::main`: the hot loop is SSE2 packed integer arithmetic (24 packed ops). rustc's default target is baseline x86-64, so this is 128-bit SSE2; `rustc -O -C target-cpu=native` widens it further. The Rust:VL multiple on this benchmark is therefore mostly SIMD WIDTH, not scalar codegen quality — VL emits no SIMD. Report it as such.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
